mechanism_claims.claim_text: Magainin, M15, R9-magainin, and R9-M15 have direct membrane activity in bacterial and model-membrane assays, including outer-membrane permeability, inner-membrane permeability, cytoplasmic membrane depolarization, and calcein release from negatively charged liposomes. The paper states that CPP conjugation did not strongly increase these membrane-disruptive effects relative to unconjugated AMPs.

entity_scope.target_scope: E. coli, S. aureus, and model liposomes depending on assay

source_locator.method_locator: xml:sec=Inner and Outer Membrane Permeability; xml:sec=Membrane Depolarization and Disruption

limitations: Direct membrane assays support membrane perturbation, but the paper cautions that these effects do not fully explain improved Gram-negative MICs of CPP conjugates.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: R9-magainin and R9-M15 show stronger LPS neutralization than unconjugated AMPs in LAL and LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 readouts, supporting LPS interaction as a contributor to improved Gram-negative activity and anti-inflammatory activity.

source_locator.method_locator: xml:sec=LPS-Neutralizing Activity; xml:sec=TNF-alpha Release and NO Production in LPS-Stimulated Cells

limitations: The assays support LPS interaction/neutralization but do not map a structural binding interface or affinity constant.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: R9-magainin and R9-M15 translocate across model lipid bilayers more effectively than unconjugated AMPs, and FITC-labeled R9-magainin enters E. coli cells in confocal microscopy.

entity_scope.target_scope: PC/PG liposomes and E. coli KCTC 1682

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=4; xml:fig=5; xml:sec=Ability of CPP-AMP Conjugates to Translocate into Liposomes; xml:sec=Confocal Laser-Scanning Microscopy

limitations: Confocal microscopy directly images FITC-labeled magainin versus FITC-labeled R9-magainin; R9-M15 translocation support comes from the liposome assay, not the E. coli image panel.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CPP-conjugated peptides, especially R9-magainin in the source figure set, show stronger plasmid-DNA retardation than unconjugated magainin, supporting a possible intracellular nucleic-acid interaction after translocation.
limitations: DNA gel retardation supports DNA binding context but does not identify a specific intracellular target or prove DNA binding is the sole bactericidal mechanism.

non_promoted_evidence.reason: Retained as phenotype_supported/secondary-target context rather than a named direct enzyme or genetic target.
Not promoted to a single mechanism; paper supports combined membrane perturbation, LPS neutralization, translocation, and DNA-binding context.
